_note: THE STREAM CONTRACT: accuracy vocabulary, the distance/interval filter, and the shape of a position (parity/F09-geo.md). BATTERY IS THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION NOBODY TESTS. A location module that accepts `distanceFilter` and then delivers every fix anyway is a battery bug shipped to every user, and it passes any test that only checks that positions arrive. So the suppression decision is a pure function judged by this corpus on all three renderers: given the last delivered fix and a new one, does this fix go to the caller. `mocked` rides on every position because a fraud-sensitive app has to be able to see it and the platforms both offer it for free.
_note_accuracy: Five words, exact case. Each maps to a real constant on each platform - never a number the module invented - and `meters` is the horizontal accuracy the word is asking for, used by the web twin (which has only a boolean enableHighAccuracy) and by the default distance filter.

accuracyFold.name: an absent accuracy takes the balanced default
an empty accuracy takes the balanced default
an unrecognised word is refused, never silently downgraded

_note_distance: The great-circle distance between two fixes, pinned so the filter means the same thing on three runtimes. Earth radius 6371008.8 m (the IUGG mean radius), haversine. Asserted within a tolerance because three languages will not agree on the last float bit and pretending otherwise makes a green suite that fails on a device.

distance.name: one ten-thousandth of a degree of latitude is about eleven metres
a bit over a hundred metres
a degree of longitude at the equator

_note_filter: distanceFilter is metres, interval is milliseconds; either alone suppresses, and a fix must satisfy BOTH to be delivered when both are set. The first fix of a session always goes out - a filter that swallows the opening position is how a map renders in the middle of the ocean.

filter.name: the first fix of a session is always delivered
no filter at all delivers everything
A FIX INSIDE THE DISTANCE FILTER IS SUPPRESSED - this is the battery bug
a fix past the distance filter is delivered
a kilometre of movement clears a one-kilometre filter
the interval boundary delivers, so an interval of N means at least N
a fix inside the interval is suppressed
a fix past the interval is delivered
both filters set means both must pass - far enough but too soon is suppressed
both filters set - long enough but not far enough is suppressed
a clock that went backwards does not permanently wedge the stream
filter._note: A device clock change or a queued fix arriving late must not make `next.at - last.at` negative forever. Treated as a fresh interval so the stream recovers.

_note_position: The position payload every renderer emits. `mocked` is a first-class field, not an extra: a delivery or wagering app has to be able to refuse a spoofed fix, iOS exposes it as CLLocation.sourceInformation.isSimulatedBySoftware and Android as Location.isMock, and surfacing it costs nothing.
_note_maxage: `last({ maxAge })` answers from the cached fix WITHOUT waking the radio, which is the entire point: a screen that only needs a rough position must never cost a GPS lock. A cache older than maxAge is a typed absence, not a stale fix returned as if it were current.

maxAge.name: a fresh cached fix is served
a stale cached fix is refused rather than passed off as current
no maxAge means any cached fix is acceptable
